entities.summary:
Alexander Lysimachus the Alabarch was a Jewish aristocrat of Alexandria, Egypt, born into a prominent family and educated in Jewish scripture and philosophy. He was a member of the Alexandrian Jewish elite and played a significant role in the Jewish community of Alexandria during the 1st century CE. His brother, Philo of Alexandria, was a renowned philosopher and exegete, and the two brothers likely collaborated on their works.

Alexander's significance lies in his involvement in the Jewish community of Alexandria, which was a melting pot of Jewish, Greek, and Egyptian cultures. He was likely influenced by the philosophical and intellectual currents of the time, which included Stoicism and Platonism. Alexander's own philosophical views are not well-documented, but his association with his brother Philo suggests that he may have been influenced by the philosophical traditions of the time.

Alexander's legacy is that of a Jewish leader who played a significant role in the Jewish community of Alexandria, which continued to thrive and evolve throughout the Roman period. His brother Philo's works, which included commentaries on the Torah and the Septuagint, had a lasting impact on Jewish thought and scholarship.

The Alabarch's influence can be seen in the preservation of Jewish texts and traditions in Alexandria, which served as a hub of Jewish learning and culture. The Alabarch's own writings, if they exist, would likely have been influenced by his brother's philosophical and exegetical works.

In the 19th century, the discovery of the Nag Hammadi library revealed a treasure trove of early Christian texts, including the Apocryphon of John, which contains references to the Alabarch and his brother Philo. This discovery provided valuable insights into the Jewish context of early Christianity and the role of Jewish leaders like the Alabarch in shaping the early Christian movement.
